steps.label: Separable con sustantivo
steps.sentence: She **turned off** the TV. / She **turned** the TV **off**.

steps.label: Separable con pronombre
steps.change: Con pronombre, la partícula va después: nunca “turned off it”.

steps.label: Inseparable
steps.sentence: She **looks after** the kids. → She **looks after** them.
steps.change: No se separa: nunca “looks them after”.

C1-1-0.title: Registro: phrasal verb vs. verbo formal

items.example: I can’t put up with the noise.
The policy does not tolerate abuse.

items.note: La primera: dejé el cigarrillo. La segunda: me detuve para fumar.
“Remember to” = no olvides hacerlo; “remember + -ing” = tengo el recuerdo.
“Try to” = haz el esfuerzo; “try + -ing” = pruébalo como solución.
“Regret to” anuncia una mala noticia; “regret + -ing” = me arrepiento de haberlo hecho.

items.b: He went on to talk about prices.
items.note: “Go on + -ing” = siguió; “go on to” = pasó a otro tema.

branches.if: enjoy, avoid, mind, suggest, deny, risk
branches.example: She denied taking the money.

branches.if: decide, hope, offer, refuse, promise, afford
branches.example: We can’t afford to wait.

branches.if: una preposición (in, at, of, instead of)
branches.example: Instead of calling, she wrote.

branches.if: stop, remember, try, regret, go on
branches.example: I’ll never forget meeting her.

steps.label: Deber futuro
steps.change: Algo que todavía hay que hacer.

steps.label: Recuerdo pasado
steps.change: La acción ocurrió antes del recuerdo.

branches.if: want, expect, tell, ask, advise, allow, get
branches.example: I want you to try this on.

branches.if: make, let, have
branches.example: They made us wait outside.

branches.if: see, hear, watch, notice (acción completa)
branches.example: I saw her leave the building.

branches.if: see, hear, watch, notice (acción en progreso)
branches.example: I saw her leaving the building.

steps.label: Sin pasiva de let
steps.change: “Let” no tiene pasiva: usa “be allowed to”.

items.note: En inglés no se usa “that” + subjuntivo con “want”.
La primera: oí toda la canción. La segunda: lo oí mientras cantaba.

C1-2-1.title: Pon el foco en la idea clave

steps.label: Destacar una acción
steps.sentence: **What she did was** change the whole design.
steps.change: Para una acción: What + sujeto + did + was (to) + verbo.

branches.if: Una cosa o idea
branches.example: What I need is a holiday.

branches.if: Una acción
branches.example: What we did was call the police.

branches.if: Un solo elemento (persona, lugar, momento)
branches.example: It was in Medellín that we met.

branches.if: Lo único, con énfasis
branches.example: All I want is some peace and quiet.

items.a: What I need is a new suit.
items.b: What I need are new shoes.
items.note: “Be” suele concordar con lo que viene después.

items.a: What she did was change the plan.
items.b: What she did was she changed the plan.
items.note: Después de “What … did was” va el verbo base (o to + verbo), sin repetir el sujeto.

items.a: What I love is the colour.
items.b: That I love is the colour.

C1-3-0.title: ¿A/an, the o nada?
C1-3-0.question: ¿Cómo es el sustantivo en tu frase?

branches.if: Singular contable, se menciona por primera vez o es uno de muchos
branches.example: A breakthrough was announced today.

branches.if: Específico, ya mencionado o único
branches.example: The breakthrough we discussed is real. / the internet

branches.if: Superlativo, ordinal u “only”
branches.example: It’s the first trial of its kind.

branches.if: Idea general en plural o incontable
branches.example: Technology changes fast. Robots are cheaper now.

branches.if: Institución con su función general (school, hospital, university)
branches.example: She’s at university. He’s in hospital.

steps.label: Segunda mención
steps.sentence: **The** test costs less than a dollar.

items.note: En general, sin artículo; con “the” hablarías de una tecnología específica.
UK: “in hospital” = internada; “the hospital” = el edificio (US usa “the” en ambos casos).
“A / an” depende del sonido, no de la letra.

steps.label: Razón
steps.sentence: **Because she felt curious**, she opened the app.

steps.label: Acción anterior
steps.sentence: **After they had tested** the device, they published the results.

steps.label: Perfecta
steps.sentence: **Having tested** the device, they published the results.

steps.label: Negativa
steps.sentence: **Not knowing** the password, he gave up.

C1-3-1.title: ¿Qué forma de -ing clause?
C1-3-1.question: ¿Qué relación hay con la acción principal?

branches.if: Ocurre al mismo tiempo o da la razón
branches.example: Feeling tired, I went to bed.

branches.if: Ocurre antes que la acción principal
branches.example: Having finished the report, she left.

branches.if: Es negativa
branches.example: Not wanting to wait, we took a taxi.

branches.if: Tiene sentido pasivo
branches.example: Shocked by the news, he sat down.

items.a: Feeling curious, she opened the app.
items.b: Feeling curious, the app was opened.
items.note: En la segunda, parece que la app sentía curiosidad.

items.a: Walking home, I saw an accident.
items.note: El sujeto de la cláusula principal debe ser quien camina.

items.a: Not knowing the answer, he stayed quiet.
items.b: Knowing not the answer, he stayed quiet.
